newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt official denies privatisation of oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Egypt official denies privatisation of oil firms.

text.p: Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi said in comments published on Tuesday the state would not privatise its oil companies or refineries because they are strategic industries that must remain under its control.
Ministry officials confirmed Banbi's comments, which were published in the official al-Ahram newspaper.

"The shares in oil firms and refineries are not up for sale through the Cairo stock exchange... these institutions perform a strategic national role and protect national interests," Banbi was quoted as saying.

Last week, the government newspaper al-Akhbar quoted Manpower and Employment Minister Ahmed el-Amawi as saying the state would retain a 60 percent holding in oil firms when it puts them up for privatisation.
Amawi's comments were the first time an official mentioned oil companies as candidates for sale to the private sector.
The state also considers the milling, defence industry and the pharmaceutical sectors as strategic.

Last year, it gave up majority control of three flour mills -- Upper Egypt Flour Mills, East Delta Flour Mills and Central and West Delta Flour Mills -- but executives at the partially privatised millers have said they will remain under state control.
Privatising one of four big state banks is on the agenda but there have been conflicting reports on which bank the state will choose and how large a stake it will sell.
